channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Thousands of Belgian military personnel share sensitive data via running app Strava
item.description: Around 4,000 service members had recorded exercise on the grounds of high-security locations, including NATO headquarters in Brussels.

item.title: Footpaths in north of Brussels get makeover to boost walking and cycling
item.description: Several paths and footpaths in Haren have been renovated as part of the City of Brussels’ efforts to improve walking and cycling connections in the neighbourhood.

item.title: Pools, dog dancing and a 400 m² scent adventure: Woofstock returns to Brussels
item.description: Visitors will also be able to take part in dog yoga, massages, workshops and talks.

item.title: Woman allegedly jumped out of window in Uccle flat on day of her eviction
item.description: The landlord reportedly obtained a court order authorising her eviction last year.

item.title: Several lanes of Brussels ring road to be closed during night next week
item.description: The works will affect two sections of the ring.

item.title: Tesla's self-driving mode showed many issue during tests in Brussels
item.description: The vehicle exceeded the legal speed limit on 55% of the tested stretches in 30 km/h zones.

item.title: Brussels expands multi-faith cemetery
item.description: "This solution will meet needs in the coming years, but we must continue to work towards a long-term, structural solution."

item.title: Is Belgium really heading back to the office?
item.description: More and more Belgian workers are abandoning the casual and cosy vibes of their homes and heading back into the office.

item.title: Brussels' Flemish representative pledges to preserve 'citizen-focused' Dutch services
item.description: He described Brussels as a place that can sometimes feel like a village, while also containing the whole world within it.

item.title: Man, 33, found with throat cut in homeless shelter in Brussels
item.description: Police are investigating the circumstances of his death.

item.title: Remote work is attracting more applicants to Brussels civil service
item.description: Remote working has a positive effect on staff retention, with employees who can work remotely around 40% less likely to leave their institution.

item.title: Investigation opened into Brussels' €55 million security spending
item.description: Some of the questioned expenses include €3 million set aside for a cybersecurity centre that was reportedly never built and a possible Disneyland trip.

item.title: Explosion damages front side of barber shop in Schaerbeek overnight
item.description: The explosion damaged the shop’s façade and shattered its window.

item.title: No agreement on extending Russian sanctions as EU deadline approaches
item.description: European Union member states have still not reached agreement on renewing sanctions against around 3,000 Russian individuals and organisations.

item.title: One injured after reported attack with 'bladed weapon' in Brussels EU Quarter
item.description: A young person was injured on Monday afternoon following an attack with a bladed weapon in the European quarter in Brussels.

item.title: Police spread images of suspects arson Anderlecht
item.description: Police have spread images of three suspects in a case of arson in the Rue Hoorickx in Anderlecht on 1 August 2026.

item.title: Brussels City Council remains undecided on Grand Casino concession
item.description: The Brussels City Council has not yet decided on the new concession holder for the Grand Casino.

item.title: One in two cigarettes smoked in Belgium is either foreign or counterfeit
item.description: More than half of cigarette packets collected in Belgium now come from abroad or are counterfeit, with the proportion rising sharply over the past year.

item.title: Brussels takes back its streets on Car-Free Sunday: 'It is a bit like a Utopia'
item.description: Cars out, people in. For nine and a half hours on Sunday, Brussels belonged to people on foot, bikes and skateboards.

item.title: 'Very serious': Two Brussels art schools file complaint against teacher who allegedly violated students
item.description: Two Brussels art schools have referred allegations of sexual violence against a former teacher to prosecutors after several female students came forward.
